english.title: Trader engage in unfair commercial practice involving contravention of requirements of professional diligence
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a trader, engaged in an unfair commercial practice likely to cause the average consumer to take a transactional decision that the consumer would not have taken otherwise as a result of the practice which involved a contravention of the requirements of professional diligence and you knew, or were reckless, as to whether the commercial practice involved a contravention of the requirements of professional diligence
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 237(4) and 240 of the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being a trader
in breach of section 225(1) of the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024
engaged in an unfair commercial practice
which involved a contravention of the requirements of professional diligence
knowing/being reckless as to whether the commercial practice involved a contravention of the requirements of professional diligence

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) For the purposes of this offence, a trader who fails to have regard to whether a commercial practice involves a contravention of the requirements of professional diligence is to be treated as being reckless as to whether it does regardless of whether the trader has reason to believe it might be, see section 237(5) of the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024.
(ii) Section 229 of the Act sets out what is considered a contravention of the requirements of professional diligence.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see section 241
